reason: The picture shows the muscle messengers meeting these cells and activating muscle genes, so this is a sensible start toward the muscle RNA goal.
expectation: The messengers should steer some cells toward using their muscle-protein instructions, possibly producing RNA copies.

alternatives.reason: That would start the other goal by activating support-protein genes.

effect: The muscle messengers produced RNA copies, and the new goal is to build the proteins they specify.
reaction: It is helpful to see the RNA copies before the proteins are made.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and these cells now have the muscle-protein instructions.
expectation: The cells should use the amino acids to build pulling proteins from the RNA instructions.

alternatives.reason: I could start the supporting-cell goal instead.

effect: The amino acids became pulling proteins inside separate muscle cells, completing that goal. The supporting-cell RNA goal remains.
reaction: The picture makes the link between the instructions and the sliding proteins clearer.
reason: The supporting-cell messengers are pictured activating support-protein genes in the unspecialized cells.
expectation: Some cells should make RNA copies of their support-protein instructions.

effect: The supporting-cell messengers produced RNA copies, revealing the goal of building fibres around the cells.
reaction: The two cell groups use different instructions despite having the same DNA.
reason: As with the muscle proteins, the cells have RNA instructions and amino acids are the protein building blocks.
expectation: The cells should use the amino acids to make supporting fibres around themselves.

effect: The cells made supporting tissue by releasing protein material around themselves, completing the last goal. This contrasts with the muscle cells keeping pulling proteins inside.
reaction: The contrast helped make the different jobs of cells with the same DNA clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the two kinds of protein was most worthwhile: the results showed pulling fibres inside muscle cells and supporting fibres around other cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second messenger-to-RNA pairing felt somewhat repetitive after the muscle pathway, although it set up the useful comparison.

surprise.text: I was struck by cells with the same DNA making different proteins, and by supporting cells releasing material around themselves.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary; the messenger pictures named the genes they activated, and amino acids were identified as protein building blocks.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, especially to see how the separate muscle cells are assembled into larger fibres, as the result hinted.
